author: _Stormz
body:
This is just a rough idea, but I have seen that there are a few posts on the forums that only get a simple "yes" or "k" response from the members of the community without actually getting a good amount of input from each person. The conversation would end right there. If it's a post regarding criticisms and opinions, instead of saying +1 or "it's good", it would be a lot better if everyone was able to provide their stance and their reasoning behind that. If a minimum character count of 50 is implemented (example), it would encourage further discussion of the topic. 

What are your thoughts on this? I'm expecting a few short responses, honestly. XD

replies.author: Kammeh
replies.body:
Honestly, I don't think this is a bad idea. The benefits of having such a system would include longer and more thorough discussions with more ideas being spread around. This will also help reduce the spam posts where lets say ten to fifteen people reply with a simple "-1, +1, I like it, it's bad, no, or k" That in turn will make the forums a more enjoyable and interesting place where every post you click on has the opinions and thoughts of other users. Furthermore, if someone is looking for something interesting or informing about the community, server or players, they will get a more complete picture in their mind, making it easier for them to stop being shy and reply. Along with these also come disadvantages though D:

I think that what will happen is forum activity might lessen at this point, (or posting at least) This would probably be because of the low traffic count of the website itself. Maybe if more players start joining the forums, this could be better suited for the forums, because large discussions will take place, making the forums more diverse and player friendly. Another problem with implementing such a rule is that there are some posts that specifically ask for a certain amount of words to be replied with. If this rule is implemented, such posts will be useless. Also, other posts cannot be answered with longs replies. Some are just a simple "Yes" or "No" seeking posts. So this rule will be a bit difficult to fit in with all of these different scenarios.

One way that this could be somewhat put into action is that staff can use their sense of judgment to decide whether or not a reply is appropriate in the given context. If it is not, maybe they can remove the post or just message the user to make sure that their replies are long enough and are not similar to spam. This is better then having some sort of actual barrier that does not allow you to post a reply if it is not long enough. Overall I think the way we handle this rule (if we actually put it into play) is with leniency, because it would be burdensome to have such strict rules restricting players from making some type of input. 

I find it kind of funny how this post is replying to one about whether there should be a limit onto how short a post can be because, this is the complete opposite of short :P
